correctness.rationale: The two-sided finite-depth genealogical construction gives a stationary law with finite second moments and backward coupling uniqueness. Stationary generator balances give \(V=2D/r\), \(\operatorname{Var}(X_n)=nV\) and \(\operatorname{Cov}(X_1,X_j)=V2^{-(j-1)}\). A lower-bidiagonal conditional-mean ODE gives both lagged covariances exactly. Strict monotonicity of Q_m proves a unique positive optimum and exact peak. A geometrically controlled root expansion yields \(z_m=m-1+O(m^{-1})\); dominated convergence and local Stirling expansion give the Gaussian pulse and \(n^{-1}\) Pearson peak. The independent finite moment-matrix/expm checker passed 728 tests. Finite checks are support, not proof of the \(n\to\infty\) statements.

value.rationale: The 2025 paper interprets the chain as lossy information transmission; the 2026 paper asks how the chain relaxes. Exact temporal source-to-depth correlations directly quantify propagation delay and direction, and the deep-chain limit overturns the naive inference from exponential equal-time attenuation: optimal delayed Pearson correlation is 1/n with a Gaussian pulse centered at linear lag and diffusive width. This specific sharp invariant measures reproducible physical timing and nonequilibrium asymmetry rather than an arbitrary subcase. It does not claim thermodynamic entropy or capacity.
